correctness.rationale: The local three-periodicity equivalence follows from all state trajectories over three transitions and connectedness. A chosen successor neighbor at each vertex yields a directed cycle length divisible by three. With only one such cycle in a cactus, any successor arrow entering a descendant block would necessarily return through its parent articulation and create a prohibited second resonant directed cycle. This justifies local independent block support. The core has exactly six oriented phase patterns; bridges each have one forced extension; a rooted length-l cycle has exactly 2 floor(l/3)+1 extensions, obtained from two explicit incremental-word families and modulo-three closure. Direct independent exhaustive three-step simulations on 193,212 labelled configurations across ten graphs, plus transfer DP for 198 rooted lengths, agree. All quantifiers and edge cases are included in RESULT.md; finite tests are not substituted for proof.

originality.rationale: No statement in the relevant inspected primary results gives the time-zero primitive-three population on singly resonant finite cactus block trees. The 2016 finite-graph theorem gives asymptotic excitation rate through contour integrals but not initial three-cycle support; the known general cactus rate distribution is a different observable. The earlier triangular-cactus-chain census concerns multiple resonant triangles, whereas the present mixed-length product applies to exactly one resonant cycle and all placements of nonresonant cycle blocks and trees. Exhaustive equivalence and dominance comparisons against the accessible records and targeted searches identified no covered form; residual priority risks are recorded.
residual_risks: Targeted searches cannot rule out all unindexed graph-coloring or cellular-automata enumeration literature.
A differently phrased cyclic-neighbor coloring theorem could subsume the rooted-product argument even without naming Greenberg–Hastings excitation.
The earlier 1993 lattice paper was examined for topic and scope, not exhaustively page by page; its object is substantially different from rooted cactus enumeration.

value.rationale: A natural, fully specified dynamical invariant—the complete initial primitive-three periodic population—is classified for all connected cacti with exactly one resonant cycle, with no fixed bound on graph size or block-tree complexity. Bridge/tree attachment invariance and multiplicative staircase factors are structural, not arbitrary tabulated numbers. It distinguishes an immediate periodicity census from prior asymptotic activity and supplies exact orbit populations for many sparse excitable-network topologies. Multiple resonant cycles are deliberately excluded because interaction between cycle supports changes the answer.
